# Code of Conduct

Project NULLWEAR is a small, focused open-source project that exists to protect the safety of serving law-enforcement officers from a real radio-frequency surveillance threat. We expect everyone participating in the project — contributors, reviewers, agencies, manufacturers, security researchers — to behave like adults engaged in serious work.

## Standards

Behaviour we expect:

- Be technically honest. If a claim isn't verified, say so. If you find a defect, surface it. The integrity of the project rests on people not bullshitting each other.
- Be respectful. Disagree with code, with claims, with designs — not with people.
- Stay focused on the work. This isn't the right project for ideological tangents about policing more broadly.
- Treat operationally sensitive information appropriately. The threat model and the asset register exist for a reason.
- If you're a public figure or have an outside role that creates real or perceived conflicts of interest, declare it.

Behaviour we do not accept:

- Harassment of any kind.
- Personal attacks, slurs, or sustained hostility.
- Doxxing or attempts to identify serving officers from project artefacts.
- Posting operational deployment information (specific locations, specific officer details, asset-register data) in any public channel.
- Attempting to bypass the secure-contact process in [`CONTACT.md`](../CONTACT.md) for cryptographic-material handoff.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies to all project spaces — GitHub issues and PRs, security advisories, project email correspondence, in-person briefings, conference presentations, and any other forum where a person is participating as a contributor or recipient of the project.

## Enforcement

If you experience or witness behaviour that violates this Code of Conduct, contact the maintainer via the channels in [`CONTACT.md`](../CONTACT.md). Reports will be:

- Acknowledged within 5 business days.
- Investigated discreetly.
- Acted upon proportionately — ranging from a private clarification, to a formal warning, to a project ban for serious or repeated violations.

The maintainer reserves the right to remove contributions, reject pull requests, or revoke access for behaviour that violates this Code, with or without warning depending on severity.

## A note for security researchers

You are very welcome here. The Vulnerability Reporting Policy in [`SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md) is the primary channel for findings. Please follow it, especially the part about not testing against deployed officer units.

---

Adapted from the principles of the Contributor Covenant, kept short and operational rather than templated. The intent is the same.
